title: Freshwater biotas evolve and go extinct more slowly, keeping relict forms

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Freshwater biotas evolve and go extinct more slowly, keeping relict forms

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because all freshwater basins together form a small area, competition among freshwater organisms has been less severe, so new forms have arisen more slowly and old forms have been exterminated more slowly there, which is why fresh water holds ancient and anomalous forms.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: All fresh-water basins, taken together, make a small area compared with that of the sea or of the land; and, consequently, the competition between fresh-water productions will have been less severe than elsewhere; new forms will have been more slowly formed, and old forms more slowly exterminated.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Circumstances favourable and unfavourable to Natural Selection, namely, intercrossing, isolation, number of individuals”. Scope: freshwater organisms, compared with marine and terrestrial ones

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The turnover and relict predictions are testable using large public fossil and phylogenetic resources. Habitat biases and the indirect inference from small area to weak competition limit causal resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare freshwater, marine and terrestrial lineages for origination, extinction, lineage age and phylogenetic distinctiveness. Slower turnover and a greater excess of old isolated lineages in freshwater support the prediction, although competition would require separate evidence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Turnover differences cannot by themselves identify competition as the cause.

Freshwater fossil preservation and sampling differ from marine records.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.67
data existence: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Habitat, diversification, and lineage age are available for fishes and for fossil marine groups, which lets a team compare environments. The freshwater fossil record is the weak part of the claim's scope, and poor preservation can manufacture an appearance of slow turnover. Phylogenetic relicts can be counted for living taxa, but that is a proxy for the historical rate claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare speciation and extinction rates, and the stem ages of living species-poor lineages, among freshwater, marine, and terrestrial clades. Lower origination and extinction in fresh water, plus an excess of old relict lineages, would confirm the claim; equal or higher freshwater rates in well-preserved groups would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Freshwater fossils are preserved less completely than marine shelly faunas.

Relict is a judgment about morphological oddity as well as phylogenetic age.

Habitat shifts move lineages across the categories being compared.
